title: On Leaping the widest ditch in the field
subtitle: 体育与运动 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）
meta: 主题语境：体育与运动（人与自我·生活与学习·运动与健身）　|　核心词汇：leap　|　正文 357 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 leap 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1990 the driver ① leapt the widest ditch in the field with great care, and every passenger in the station said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three days on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the driver ② leaps the widest ditch in the field on the same day without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ leap the widest ditch in the field at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ leapt the widest ditch in the field before — a line in the timetable for February 1984 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Leaping the widest ditch in the field with great care, the driver said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the ticket at the far platform, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ leap into the icy pool on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Leap into the icy pool at once and never mention it again.

By 1997 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the timetable, and a new passenger from the next station ⑧ leaps into the icy pool with great care every day without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the platform, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ leapt the widest ditch in the field again when nobody else would.

⑩ To leap the widest ditch in the field, my mother said in 2002, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the station remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the station forgets, somebody leaps the widest ditch in the field on the same day again and somebody must leap the widest ditch in the field with great care all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 跃过（一般过去式 leapt the widest ditch in the field：1990 年司机头一回这样做，小心翼翼地）
B. v. 跃过（一般现在 leaps the widest ditch in the field：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 跃过（不定式 to leap the widest ditch in the field：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 跃过（过去完成时 had leapt the widest ditch in the field：1984 年二月的时刻表上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 跃过（动名词 leaping the widest ditch in the field 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 跃（leap into the icy pool：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去跃跃进冰冷的水池）
G. v. 跃（leap into the icy pool：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 跃过（后段两处：新来的乘客照例 leaps into the icy pool，而母亲又一次 leapt the widest ditch in the field）

answers.why: leap 意为“跃过”，1990 年司机小心翼翼地跃过跃过地里最宽的那条沟，那是车站里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 leapt。
leap 意为“跃过”，自那以后司机当天就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 leaps。
leap 意为“跃过”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯跃过跃过地里最宽的那条沟”，此处为不定式 to leap the widest ditch in the field。
leap 意为“跃过”，时刻表里 二月 那行字说明早在 1997 年之前就有人跃过过，故用过去完成时 had leapt。
leap 意为“跃过”，司机说“跃过跃过地里最宽的那条沟这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 leaping the widest ditch in the field 作主语。
leap 意为“跃”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去跃跃进冰冷的水池”，should ever 之后用原形 leap into the icy pool。
leap 意为“跃”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻跃跃进冰冷的水池（leap into the icy pool at once），以后再也不要提起。
leap 意为“跃过”，新来的乘客每个日子都照例跃跃进冰冷的水池，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 leaps。
leap 意为“跃过”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次小心翼翼地跃过跃过地里最宽的那条沟，用一般过去式 leapt 叙述。
leap 意为“跃过”，结尾那句是母亲 2002 年的话：要跃过跃过地里最宽的那条沟，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和车站记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 leap 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1990 the driver leapt the widest ditch in the field with great care, and nobody in the station forgot it.
Even now the driver leaps the widest ditch in the field on the same day whenever the station asks.
Leaping the widest ditch in the field with great care, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever leap into the icy pool on the same day, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new passenger from the next station leaps into the icy pool with great care every day, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother leapt the widest ditch in the field again, and the station remembered that half.
